question: The distance from the center \(O\) to line \(l\) is 6. The radius \(r\) of circle \(O\) is an integer, and \(l\) and circle \(O\) are disjoint. Find the maximum value of \(r\).
solution: For the line and circle to be disjoint, \(d>r\), so \(r<6\). The maximum integer value of \(r\) is 5.

edges.reason: Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.
The meaning of a value satisfying an equation is an analogy for inequality solutions. Directly testing x>3 uses order without equation background.
edges.scope: meaning of a solution by analogy

edges.reason: A signed numerical inequality expresses an order relation, so the meaning of greater/less is part of interpreting it.
The general modeling routine transfers, but at-least/at-most relations and admissible integer solutions can be taught directly in inequalities; the equality-modeling family is preparation.
The modeled one-variable inequality must be solved before feasible quantities can be interpreted.
The threshold distance is the shortest perpendicular center-to-line segment.

The target explicitly connects line position with intersection count and center-distance thresholds. The inside/on/outside meaning for the line points is used in that explanation, without requiring every earlier exercise.
edges.scope: Explaining line-circle intersection counts using inside, on and outside points
